payload.headline: Alphabet: sales growth is speeding up, but free cash flow has collapsed

summary.thesis: The business is growing faster and keeping more profit from each sale, but free cash flow has fallen from 73.6B to 19.7B, analysts are cutting this year's earnings forecasts, and the price of 293.45 sits above the middle of its own historical valuation range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a better price or for cash flow to recover; swing: wait, because the price is pressing against a well-tested ceiling.
summary.act_at: near 282.31, or in the 275.71–278.28 support zone

payload.happening: GOOGL closed at 293.45, up 2.11% on the day, and was at 295.77 intraday at 10:54 ET (not a close). That puts it inside a price ceiling at 293.72–296.49 that has turned the stock back 4 times, and it is still below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (308.18, 329.88, 338.59). The news is mostly product launches that were reported and confirmed: Gemini 4 Carbon, two new specialized AI chips and AI glasses. No earnings date is in the data.
payload.business: What changes the business: sales are growing faster, at 24.65% a year in the latest quarter compared with 21.79% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, edged up to 33.32% from 32.19%. The real worry is cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, a free-cash-flow margin of just 4.19%. Heavy spending on AI data centers is the usual reason for a drop like this (general knowledge), so the open question is whether that spending will pay off. Net margin of 50.03% is well above operating margin, which suggests one-off gains outside the core business are boosting profit (general knowledge). Treat headline earnings with care for that reason. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 139.0B and liquidity is 265.1B. The chip, Gemini and glasses news and OpenAI's push into business profiles mainly move sentiment and the story about competition. On their own they do not change today's numbers. What is at risk: the earnings path. This year's EPS estimate fell 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's consensus of 14.97 is below this year's 19.56.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply, and one assumption explains most of the gap. The cash-flow model (DCF) starts from free cash flow of only 19.7B and gives 26.28 / 52.56 / 72.2 per share. Even at 30% starting growth it reaches only 80.15. On that basis the price looks far too high: the filings-based risk note says the price needs about 37% a year growth, against 17% a year delivered over 3 years. Measured against its own past price-to-sales ratios, Alphabet is worth 234.35 / 282.31 / 375.22, so 293.45 is a little above the middle. Against peers it looks expensive, with price-to-sales of 7.7 versus a peer median of 5.4. On earnings it looks cheap, at 15.4 times trailing EPS and 15.0 times this year's EPS. But that earnings figure is inflated by the gap between net and operating margin, and the next-year multiple rises to 19.6. I treat the own-history range as the usable anchor and discount the DCF, because its cash base sits at a low point caused by heavy spending.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the prior 73.6B once AI spending pays off. If it stays near 19.7B, even the 234.35 low is generous.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales growth reached 24.65% from 21.79% two quarters ago, and trailing revenue rose to 471.1B from 385.5B.
Profitability is improving: operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19% while R&D still takes 15.81% of revenue.
The balance sheet is strong, with 139.0B of net cash, and the trailing earnings multiple of 15.4 is low for a company growing 22.21%.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, and on that cash base the DCF base case is just 52.56 per share.
Analysts are cutting forecasts: this year's EPS estimate fell 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's consensus (14.97) is below this year's (19.56).
It is expensive against peers, at a price-to-sales ratio of 7.7 versus a peer median of 5.4, and the price is below its falling 50-day average of 329.88.

levels.what: Middle of its own historical price-to-sales range, the fair-value anchor
Top of the 275.71–278.28 support zone, which has held twice
Low end of its own-history range, a margin of safety if cash flow stays weak

longterm.why: The business is good (grade B), but the price is above my fair-value range and forecasts are falling. A pullback toward 282.31 or a recovery in free cash flow would improve the trade-off.

swing.why: The price is inside resistance at 293.72–296.49, which has capped it 4 times, and the trend is a range below falling averages. That leaves little room to the upside before the next ceiling at 300.07–305.86 and no clean setup.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in the data, so timing depends on forecast revisions and price levels. Options price a move of about 8.0% by Dec 18, and the busiest put strike is at 290.0, which marks it as a level traders are watching.

change_mind: A daily close above the 300.07–305.86 resistance zone would break the range and argue for a more constructive stance.
A filing showing trailing free cash flow climbing back from 19.7B toward 73.6B would close the gap between the DCF and history-based values.
A break below the 269.6–272.17 support zone, or further cuts to this year's EPS estimate beyond the 5.2% 30-day drop, would push the stance toward avoid.
